result.title: Preserve to Compress: Beyond Low-Dimensional Latents in One-Step Diffusion Codec
result.summary: Pretrained latent diffusion models bring powerful generative priors to ultra-low-bitrate image compression, but their latent spaces reflect a reconstruction--generation tradeoff. Low-dimensional latents reduce modeling cost but can discard image details, while higher-dimensional latents improve reconstruction yet make diffusion optimization harder under a fixed computational budget. Generative codecs that adopt these pretrained spaces also inherit this compromise, even though compression requires fidelity to a specific source image. In particular, low-dimensional latent interfaces can discard source details before coding and restrict how much decoded information reaches the image decoder. We propose Preserving Information for Compression and Synthesis (PICS), a one-step generative image compression framework that adapts these interfaces to preserve source information. Our Information-Preserving Adaptors (IPAs) expose richer features for coding and retain decoded information throughout reconstruction, while deferred decoder adaptation stabilizes training and helps the image decoder exploit the expanded representations. Experiments on Kodak, DIV2K, and CLIC 2020 show average BD-rate savings of 52.64% and 39.61% over StableCodec at matched LPIPS and DISTS, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PICS 一步扩散图像压缩框架，用信息保持适配器改造预训练 latent 接口，使编码端获得更丰富特征并在解码全程保留信息，以缓解低维 latent 的细节丢失。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文对「低维 latent 接口在编码前即丢弃源细节、限制信息到达解码器」的分析及适配器式信息保持设计，可能为 LVR 中视觉细节是否留在内部状态、latent 维度与信息坍缩的关系提供类比线索，需核查其信息度量方式。
